description:
## Finding
\`pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:713\`:
\`\`\`rust
fn cert_is_ca_cert(cert: &Certificate) -> bool {
    cert.tbs_certificate.extensions.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])
        .iter()
        .find(|e| e.extn_id == OID_BASIC_CONSTRAINTS)
        .and_then(|e| BasicConstraints::from_der(e.extn_value.as_bytes()).ok())
        .is_some_and(|bc| bc.ca)
}
\`\`\`

The \`.ok()\` discards a \`der::Error\`. A cert with a present-but-malformed BasicConstraints is silently treated as not-a-CA.

## Why P2
- \`cert_is_ca_cert\` drives the IDP scope check in \`check_revocation\` (lines 273–286). If a cert is actually a CA but has a malformed BC, this routine returns \`false\`, so a CRL with \`only_contains_ca_certs=true\` will be silently skipped (return \`Ok(())\` at line 281–284) — the CRL is treated as not covering that cert when in reality it should.
- The corresponding pkix-path code (\`try_find_cert_ext\`) is fail-closed for security-critical extension decoding. This crate inconsistently fail-opens.
- Documented elsewhere as risk: \`MalformedCertificate\` is the typical error variant for this case.

## Fix
Change \`cert_is_ca_cert\` to return \`crate::Result<bool>\` and return \`Err(Error::CrlParseError(...))\` (or a new variant) on malformed BC. Both call sites in \`check_revocation\` (line 273) and \`check_revocation_against_anchor\` (line 401) need the propagation.

Alternatively, follow pkix-path's policy: malformed extension → MalformedCertificate-equivalent error, propagate up through the revocation path.

## Scope reference
\`pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:713-724\`, callers at lines 273, 401.
title: P2: cert_is_ca_cert in pkix-revocation/crl.rs silently fail-opens on malformed BasicConstraints
